_doc: The closure ledger (campaign spec 2026-08-31-reforge-full-campaign-design.md, S1.1/S1.3/S5; contract X2). One row per in-scope subsystem and per headless catalog tool. Canonical row list: reforge/ledger/rows.ts. Validate: npx tsx ledger/check.ts. Every wave child updates its rows in its landing commit; pin bumps flip touched rows to 'stale'.

rows.title: Tool result formatters (Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, task family)
rows.note: TEN of the graph's 44 `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam` methods are excised and delegated to reforge-owned modules (Write, Glob, TaskCreate from M3-B; Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate from C4/W1), 6,568 minified chars. Every one of the ten owned MODULES is standalone-complete and registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts: it ships its own constants and pure helpers, and only typed ports cross the adapter (Read's WeakMap+clock staleness prefix and tab-separator gate, Bash's background output path and task-ack envelope/ending, TaskUpdate's two agent-team predicates). The SUBSYSTEM row nevertheless stays `spliced`, not `standalone-complete`: 34 formatters remain, so the family is not owned. Coverage is honest too — the corpus renders one of Read's six result arms, one of Grep's three and the plain stdout path of Bash's six, and never truncates a Glob result; the arms it cannot reach are graded by strangle/contracts.test.ts (135 checks). DEPENDENCY EDGES (§2.4), one per effectful-port capture that leaves this row: `tool/Read` — the Read formatter's staleness prefix is a module WeakMap keyed by the result object and populated inside the Read tool's CALL path, then rendered through a Date.now()-derived day count, so it is a side channel owned by Read's execution, not data this wave can own; `subsystem/bash-executor` — the Bash formatter's background output path reads the live outputPathBindings registry, and its task-ack envelope/ending reach the background-task machinery §1.1 files under the Bash executor; `subsystem/subagent-dispatch` — TaskUpdate's completion nudge is gated on the session's agent/team identity. Read's tab-separator capture is a feature gate, and gates are neither spliced nor excluded (§3.3), so it is a port with no edge.

rows.title: Tool-result validators (Edit's validateInput and its 19 siblings)
rows.note: Split out of §1.1's 'formatters + validators' row by C4 with measured evidence: the Edit tool's error results ("String to replace not found in file.", "File has not been read yet.", the stale-read and match-count messages) are NOT produced by `mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam`. They are returned by a sibling `async validateInput`, 3,317 minified chars against the formatters' 155-1,590, carrying filesystem reads, readFileState access, `tengu_edit_tool_stale_read` telemetry and gate reads — mostly `effectful-port` captures. It needs its own scenario (a deliberately missing `old_string`) and its own gate row, so C4 scoped it out rather than smuggling it in behind a formatter wave. 20 `validateInput` methods exist in chunk-fy12d89p.js. OPEN: this row is filed under C4 because that is the child that subdivided it, and C4 does not close it — the roadmap owes it a wave assignment (campaign spec Revision Notes, 2026-09-01).

rows.note: C5/W2 owns FOUR description functions and ONE satellite chunk whole. The row's charter is wider than that on purpose, and it is not met: chunk-y30v0ja7 is reforge-owned end to end (the campaign's first S-chunk: 3 exports, 0 upstream bytes), but the Read, Grep and WebFetch chunks carry 15/17/4 exports of unrelated behaviour -- PDF page-range parsing, the REPL registry, the deferred-tool policy, the WebFetch answering prompt -- and stay upstream's, so only their description functions are spliced. The catalog also has description functions beyond these four. 'standalone-complete' would therefore be an overclaim; every owned module IS standalone-complete individually and registered in engine-ts/modules/index.ts, which is what closes the dual-wiring half. Edges are the four typed ports the descriptions take from the graph: leanPrompt (system-prompt policy), subagentSteer (subagent dispatch, latching), pdfCapable (reads the session model, hence the query-loop row) and cacheTtlPhrase (the WebFetch cache TTL). The row stays `spliced` rather than standalone-complete: the SECTION BUILDERS behind the preset's 27 KB block (upstream OS() and its ~45 free variables) are still upstream's, and so is the per-tool serializer Eie, which the scout measured as not a clean seam and referred to the tool-runtime wave. The static-prompt gate is pinned false by S3.3, so two of the partition's three paths are graded by strangle/prompt-parity.test.ts rather than by the corpus; attestation/coverage.md records all 38 exclusions with that oracle named. Two typed-port edges leave the row: the message constructor that stamps uuid and timestamp onto the system-reminder message (session/transcript), and the prompt-cache-control builder plus the remaining-token attachment (query loop). rows.title: Compaction: summarization prompt, compact_boundary emit, trigger policy

captures.name: bg
captures.note: exporting module 'crypto' is not part of the graph — only the import site is covered

rows.note: W4 owns the client-side compaction surface EXCEPT its drivers. Five splices: the summarization prompt (C5x's variable-declarator spike, graded by the build-time comparison against the pinned chunk's bytes), the compact_boundary constructor (upstream H1, both triggers rendered - 'manual' by slash-compact/compact-continue, 'auto' by auto-compact-threshold), the boundary's wire shaping (rSe, zero captures), the post-compaction continuation message together with the summary rewriter it calls (Cq + d1n in one owned module: d1n is a pure helper with one caller, so a separate splice of it was measurably dead - its solo sabotage came back GREEN), and the auto-compaction trigger predicate (nKn, 10 captures). EDGES: session-storage owns the identity minting behind the boundary's uuid; the query loop owns the context accounting the trigger reads (contextTokens, charsPerToken, classifyContextLevel, effectiveWindow) AND the compaction drivers themselves. NOT owned, and why: the DRIVERS (upstream zRe, the async generator that routes a true decision through the reactive path, and Tte, the reactive driver that runs the PreCompact hooks and calls the summarizer) are query-loop-shaped and deferred to C16/W13 with the rest of the turn driver; the summarization-prompt WRAPPERS (nie/hRt) share a byte-identical five-line preamble inside one chunk, which no coLiteral can separate; and MICROCOMPACTION is a reviewed exclusion rather than a scenario debt - createContextHintController returns null unless querySource starts with 'repl_main_thread' and the headless driver sends 'sdk', so the controller is null, onRequestError short-circuits and v4n can never run. Grading it would need the synthetic response corpus plus a patched querySource, i.e. an engine-behaviour change rather than fault injection.

rows.note: W5 owns the DISPATCHERS: twenty entry points covering TWENTY-ONE of the twenty-three hook events the engine is measured to fire headlessly (one function serves Stop and SubagentStop; the two model-switch dispatchers are the gap named below). Each owns one event's hook-input record -- its field set and ORDER, which is the byte stream a command hook reads on stdin -- plus the guard that decides whether to dispatch at all and the options the executor is asked for. THREE SHAPES: thirteen are async generators that stream their executor's results into the conversation; six await a second executor (AE) because their callers have no conversation left to stream into -- and tz/PreCompact goes further, reducing its results to a verdict the compactor obeys (custom instructions, a display message, a blocking reason), which is the only place in this subsystem where hook OUTPUT is behaviour rather than a stream; and CUt/FileChanged is neither async nor a generator, reaching NEITHER executor -- it returns the watcher-hooks helper's promise for its caller to chain. Six distinct upstream pure helpers came with them as owned helpers rather than ports, captured ten times across the rows: the hook fan-out rule and its two agent-context predicates (strangle/modules/shared/hook-agent-context.js), the last-assistant-message pair (strangle/modules/shared/assistant-text.js), and the plain-object test that decides chain eligibility. The row is SPLICED, not standalone-complete, and the gap has TWO halves. (1) THE SHARED EXECUTORS: the 23 KB generator executor (upstream Qxt, reached through jy/Xxt), its awaiting sibling AE, and the watcher-hooks helper zxt that FileChanged and CwdChanged share -- hook matching, command/callback/http/mcp invocation, timeouts, cancellation -- which the W5-W7 scout measured S-MODULE-shaped and which S2.3 says is owned behind a designed port rather than transcribed. Whichever wave takes them inherits getMatchingHooks (Rzn), the agent-context result filter (Xxt) and the headless-suppression wrapper (jy) with them. (2) THE TWO MODEL-SWITCH DISPATCHERS, mdt/PreModelSwitch and gdt/PostModelSwitch, which FIRE headlessly (measured on a /model turn) and are deliberately not spliced. They are the family's only stateful members: between them they reach a plugin loader, a model prefetch and validation preamble, a per-session decision holder that gdt MUTATES (landedOn, a pending queue, an inFlight promise set) and a fire-and-forget promise the caller never awaits -- roughly seventeen forwarded ports each. S2.3 puts a stateful core behind a designed port rather than transcribing it, and doubling this subsystem's capture inventory for two events is not that design. Recorded here so the remainder is a decision rather than an omission. WHICH EVENTS FIRE, MEASURED THREE TIMES, AND THE MEASUREMENT WAS THE HARD PART. The wave's first probe drove ONE batched tool turn with CALLBACKS only and reported eight live events. C8's boundary review found that negative vacuous -- the turn created none of the missing firing conditions -- and re-measured TWELVE. C8's second round found the re-measurement still choosing its own watched list by judgment, so three live events (PostCompact, TaskCreated, Notification) sat outside the measurement entirely and six more were never asked. The population now comes from upstream's own dispatcher registry (33 events, snapshotted as research/fixtures/hook-registry-2.1.251.json and re-derived by the gate), with one named firing condition per event: TWENTY-THREE fire, none of the created conditions came back dead, and ten stay OPEN with their conditions named rather than being counted as negatives. THE MECHANISM CLAIM IS CORRECTED. The boundary round's story -- that a callback reaches a dispatcher only if that dispatcher hands the executor a session hooks registry -- is refuted by the bundle. Options.hooks entries are NOT registry entries: the initialize handler tags them origin:sdkHost and pushes them into a global store, and the lookup every executor performs (IE, chunk-fy12d89p offset 538966) returns that store's entry for the event unconditionally, merged with the settings layers. SessionStart's callback silence is a TIMING artifact -- its dispatch precedes host-hook registration -- not structural unreachability. What remains true is the byte fact underneath it: vUt, tz and EE call their executor with no registry, which is why the owned modules forward none. No claim is made about SDK-declared events outside the registry: nothing outside it can fire. Edges, all effectful ports: the working-directory reader and the base hook-input builder (session identity + app state), the child agent's transcript path (session storage), the background-task registry's wire projection and the session cron list (moat tools / subagent dispatch), and the three execution helpers. The row's title says "+ hooks chunks" and the census that named them was WRONG (W5-W7 scout S0, re-measured): chunk-7g4v1yq9 is a bundle-wide constants chunk with 521 consumers, chunk-x5kv85y3 is the remote device-hook templates and off the headless path, and chunk-scxwkz2z is a pure named-export barrel over the engine chunk with zero code of its own -- though it is not inert: the app's own shutdown() reaches SessionEnd through it by dynamic import, which is the third SessionEnd caller and the one the ordinary-teardown fire comes from. There is no hooks chunk to own; every implementation is a free function in chunk-fy12d89p.js, which is why W5 is pure S-method.

rows.title: Permission decisions + rule matching/parsing
rows.note: W6 owns the decision chain from the pre-check down, the mode axis end to end, and the headless broker's return leg: eight splices here plus C5x's deny-stamping link, and FOUR owned functions in shared/ that are deliberately not rows. The ask-rule predicate and the safety-check finder are takeable and were measured INERT under solo sabotage, because their remaining upstream callers are gate-dead. The message builder (ql, 45 call sites) is different: it RUNS on every tool call and its output is absorbed before it reaches any observable a headless corpus can produce — an ask's message never travels to the SDK host, and the one path on which it reaches the model takes the rule checker's annotating arm, which keeps the tool's own message. All three are graded against upstream's bytes by the parity oracle, and two control_response envelopes recorded on subsystem/control-protocol. A FIFTH was measured DARK and dropped in the same way: Uct/classifierOnlyStreakActive runs on the allow arm of every tool call in every mode, and its answer is pinned false by the disabled streak gate, so the maximal twin — return true always — leaves both covering scenarios byte-identical; the row had been carried as live on a RED the gate inferred from a non-zero exit rather than from a graded verdict. A FOURTH function was measured off the headless path and dropped outright: K0/setPermissionModeWithGuards joins the guard to the transition and reads like the set_permission_mode seam, but the headless runtime's handler calls the guard DIRECTLY and applies the mode itself, so even a twin that refused every mode change left a mode walk green. Its two ends are both owned and both live, so only the joint is unowned. Graded by strangle/permissions-parity.test.ts (2,488 comparisons, 45 controls) over the axes research/fixtures/permission-surface-2.1.251.json derives from the bundle: six modes, three rule behaviours, eleven decisionReason kinds. THREE NAMED GAPS, all deferrals rather than omissions. (1) `von`, the 11.6 KB mode-aware decision body ABOVE the pre-check: sixty free variables, a model-classifier call, a mutable per-session denial counter — a §2.3 designed port, not a transcription. (2) `createCanUseTool`, the broker's own class method: five mutable maps on its receiver plus thirty-five module imports, the same shape. (3) `Dd`, the chain's two-line entry point, carries no string literal at all and is not takeable by the anchor mechanism; both of its neighbours are owned. A fourth, `eln`/initializeToolPermissionContext (5.4 KB, sixty free variables, filesystem and settings I/O), belongs with the settings layer rather than with the decision chain. The row cannot close on any of them.

rows.title: Control-protocol switch (control_request/control_response subtypes)
rows.note: W6 took the two response ENVELOPES ahead of W7, because the can_use_tool round trip is the only control request the permission chain itself issues and leaving the return leg unowned would have stopped that chain's ownership mid-round-trip. Sixteen call sites between them, zero free variables each, and every headless control_response passes through one or the other — `initialize` is the first request of every SDK-driven run, so sabotaging either reddens the whole corpus. What W7 inherits is the REQUEST leg: the 55-arm subtype dispatch inside runHeadless and the named handlers its live arms delegate to.
